subject: Clearwave renewal readiness: usage consolidation & upgrade path
messages:
From: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@clearwave.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: priya@clearwave.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick check: renewal numbers and options

Markus / team —

We’re starting planning for next year’s budget and wanted a clear picture of our usage trajectory and options for a term that reduces unit cost without sacrificing the bursts we rely on for peak nights. Can you share last six-week token cadence, anything unusual in latency/availability, and a sketch of what a 12-month commited package vs a 6-month bridge would look like cost-wise?

Also, we saw a few latency spikes on 8/11 during our batch jobs — grateful for any quick notes on root cause.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Sellers
Head of Platform, Clearwave Health
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@clearwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check: renewal numbers and options

Tom — thanks for the note. Summary below; attaching a concise usage report and a draft SOW with two term options (SOW_Draft_v3.docx).

Highlights (last 6 weeks; consolidated):
- Average daily tokens: 12.4M (±14%) — monthly run-rate ~372M tokens.
- Peak day (8/11): 45M tokens — correlates with batch ingestion and model retrain pipeline.
- Spend (hosted): ~$34.2k/month over June–Aug; effective cost per 1k tokens: $0.092 today.
- Performance: 95th pct generation latency on your primary route: 220ms (steady), but 8/11 spikes hit ~1.5s during the batch window when concurrent KV-cache warmups and large-batch reruns overlapped.
- Errors: transient 503s during the same window (0.06% of requests) — infra mitigated via autoscale; root cause: concurrent burst + cold caches on Canary pool. We throttled a downstream job and added a short pre-warm; incidents resolved within 18 minutes.

Proposed commercial options (high level):
1) 12-month committed package (recommended if you want unit-cost stability):
   - Commit: 450M tokens/mo (20% uplift vs current run-rate to cover growth)
   - Effective price: $0.078 / 1k tokens (≈15% reduction)
   - Included: 10% burst buffer, 99.9% availability SLO, quarterly performance review, one optimization credit (batching/quantization consultation).
2) 6-month bridge (flexible, lower commitment):
   - Commit: 300M tokens/mo, month-to-month after 6 months
   - Effective price: $0.086 / 1k tokens, bursts billed at overage rate with pre-agreed surge cap
   - Included: prioritized support during scheduled batch windows, single perf tuning workshop.

ROI note: If Clearwave converts to the 12-month package and maintains current spend trajectory, unit cost drops ~15% and predictable capacity reduces cost of engineering mitigation (we estimate ~$12–18k/month saved in ops/dev time for your platform team).

Next steps I'd suggest: quick internal sync (30m) to review the SOW and pick a preferred term, then we can get procurement language aligned with legal. I can loop in solutions engineering if you want a deeper look at burst pre-warming.

Attachments: Clearwave_Usage_Report_Aug2026.pdf, SOW_Draft_v3.docx

—
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@clearwave.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check: renewal numbers and options

Tom — quick add from ops / renewal side. A couple short points to help procurement:

- If you pick the 12-month commit, we can include a one-time migration credit to offset integration work for your offline pipelines (up to $6k).
- We’ll put the 10% burst buffer in the SOW as an explicit clause with a simple overage trigger (sends alerts at 85% utilization).
- For the 8/11 spike, we recommend scheduling pre-warm for monthly large-batch jobs — we’ll provide a 90-day playbook if you move to the committed package.

If helpful, Jordan and I can draft the procurement checklist (PO cadence, billing contact, and SLA exception handling) after your internal sync.

Laura Bennett
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@clearwave.com>, Priya Singh <priya@clearwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check: renewal numbers and options — proposed next steps

Tom / Priya — following up with concrete next steps based on the above: 

1) Internal decision: please confirm preferred term (12M commit or 6M bridge) by Tue 8/31.
2) If 12M, we’ll:
   - Share a redline-ready SOW (SOW_Draft_v3.docx) for your legal/procurement by EOD Mon;
   - Schedule a 45m solutions call to walk pre-warm/playbook and perf credits (options Tues/Wed).
3) If 6M bridge, we’ll:
   - Send a bridge SOW that includes prioritized support windows and monthly usage check-ins.

I’ll also circulate the usage PDF to your platform engineering Slack #platform-ops so they have the charts handy. If you want, Jordan can run a 30m runbook review with your infra team to lock the pre-warm cadence.

Can you confirm a preferred weekday/time for a sync next week?

Thanks — and happy to jump on a call if that’s faster.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
